title: The canonical finite-cycle projection is epic with its intrinsic alpha-image kernel
statement: Let C be an abelian category and X a type-zero bigraded exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple]. Fix r natural and p,q integer. Suppose D_r(p+2,q-1) is zero and initialG at (p,q) factors through Z_r of [def-sp-convergence]. Its lift followed by the canonical tower projection onto E_r is epimorphic. Its kernel is the pullback along alphaIter r from D(p,q) to D(p-r,q+r) of the image of incomingAlphaIter (r+1) at (p-r,q+r). No half-plane or colimit hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the canonical epimorphisms e_n from original D(p,q) to D_n(p-n,q+n) by identity at zero and successive image epimorphisms of restricted alpha. Using pageCouple_image, compose each with the canonical monic inclusion and obtain alphaIter n by induction.

Induct on n to identify e_n followed by transported derived g with the finite factorThru(initialG) followed by projection n. At zero apply projection_zero. At a successor apply DerivedMaps.g_comm, cancel the kernel inclusion using cycleLift_comm, and apply projection_succ. The cycle arrow is mono so the chosen lift equals factorThru. The successor cycle lift restricts to the preceding one by cancellation of its cycle arrow.

Exactness identifies the kernel of g_n with the incoming restricted-alpha image. Under the monic inclusion I_n its image is incomingAlphaIter(n+1), by the successor image recurrence. Pulling this back along e_n, whose inclusion composite is alphaIter n, gives the displayed kernel formula. The zero following D term makes f_n zero, hence exactness makes g_n epic. Since e_n is epic, the canonical finite cycle map is epic.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteCycle_kernel_presentation (X : BigradedExactCouple C 0)
    (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ)
    (hnext : IsZero ((X.pageCouple r).D (p + 2) (q - 1)))
    (hg : (X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z r p q).Factors (X.initialG p q)) :
    Epi ((X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z r p q).factorThru (X.initialG p q) hg ≫
      X.cycleBoundaryTower.projection r p q) ∧
    kernelSubobject ((X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z r p q).factorThru
        (X.initialG p q) hg ≫ X.cycleBoundaryTower.projection r p q) =
      (Subobject.pullback (X.alphaIter r p q)).obj
        (imageSubobject (X.incomingAlphaIter (r + 1) (p - r) (q + r)))
